approach: By symmetry the triangle stays equilateral while shrinking, so find the constant rate at which side AB shortens using the components of the two particles' velocities along AB.

steps.text: By the symmetry of the three particles' motion, the triangle they form stays equilateral at every instant while it shrinks and rotates about the centroid.
steps.equation: the interior angle at every vertex stays 60° throughout the motion

steps.text: Particle A moves along AB with speed v, so its full velocity v is directed along AB, reducing the separation AB at rate v.
steps.equation: component of A's velocity along AB = v

steps.text: Particle B moves along BC with speed v. Since the angle between BA and BC is 60°, B's velocity has a component along BA (toward A) equal to v cos 60°.
steps.equation: component of B's velocity toward A = v cos 60° = v/2

steps.text: The rate at which the distance AB shortens is the sum of these two components, and this rate stays constant because the 60° angle never changes.
Since AB shortens at the constant rate 3v/2 starting from side d, the particles meet when AB reaches zero.
steps.why_this_step: A quantity decreasing at a constant rate from d to 0 takes time equal to the initial value divided by the rate.

final_answer.value: The three particles meet at time t = 2d/(3v).

common_mistakes.text: Using only the direct closing speed v (ignoring the second particle's component toward the first) gives a meeting time of d/v instead of the correct 2d/(3v).
